Bug_Details:
The likely intention of a user calling Thread.run() is to start the execution of code within a new thread. This, however, is not what
happens when this method is called.
The purpose of Thread.run() is to provide a method that users can overwrite to specify the code to be executed. The actual thread is
then started by calling Thread.start() . When Thread.run() is called directly, it will be executed as a regular method within
the current thread.
Bug_Explanation: The code directly calls the run() method of the Thread object instead of start(). This means the run() method's code is executed in the current thread, not in a new thread as likely intended.

This results in the run method being executed in the main thread instead of a new thread. The test expects the message to be 'Running in a new thread!', but since Thread.run() is called directly, the message remains 'No execution', causing the test to fail.
